profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC10 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

reading.body:
Equinix DC10 is a 84,830 square foot facility in Ashburn, Virginia, part of Equinix's 15-facility Washington DC metro region. The operator publishes N+1 redundancy for cooling and generators with over 30 hours of fuel autonomy at full load, but does not publish the megawatt capacity of this building. Without a power figure, the facility's scale relative to AI infrastructure demand cannot be determined from published sources.

This facility sits in Virginia, a state with 326 mapped data centers, though only 23 publish power capacity totaling 1,375.4 megawatts. DC10 ranks outside the top 23 published facilities in the state, meaning its capacity, if disclosed, would not place it among Virginia's largest. The Ashburn corridor itself is established as North America's largest peering point and a primary gateway to Europe, but this designation reflects the metro region's collective role rather than any single building's capacity.

The absence of published megawatts for DC10 is itself meaningful. Equinix publishes capacity selectively; the lack of a figure suggests either that power density is not a primary marketing attribute for this facility tier, or that competitive considerations keep the number private. For readers assessing which facilities matter to AI scaling, this building cannot be ranked against others without additional data from the operator.
